learned_path_model: v1 GBM (model/models, sensitivity.json); relative changes only
lever: X% of upstream row-crop acres (both intake basins) add a cereal-rye-type living cover Oct-May, on top of current practice
method: What-if replay on the MEASURED river: each day's nitrate is cut by a share that combines Iowa trial results (INRS 2024: cereal rye cuts drainage nitrate 28% on average, SD 26%; applied Oct-Jul, scaled by the row-crop share of river nitrate) and our satellite-trained river model's response to less bare soil (Oct 15-May 31). The two lines of evidence get equal weight (half the simulations use each), so ranges span both. Plant and ban days use proxy rules fitted to 2025 and tested on 2026. Adoption is on top of today's ~17% (statewide) and assumes adopters are typical fields; the river may take more than one season to respond (legacy nitrate).

method_detail.quantiles: p50 = median; lo/hi = 10th/90th percentile of draws (8 in 10)
method_detail.impact_basis: relative change applied to the OBSERVED daily concentration, C'(t) = C_obs(t) x (1 - D(t)); flow unchanged; counts on measured days only; loads use measured flow x gap-filled concentration
method_detail.avoided: computed inside each draw (baseline minus scenario), then summarised

path_a_trial.formula: daily cut on Oct-Jul days = X * e * s; annual load cut dL = X * e * s * w

e.dist: normal truncated to [0,1], location solved so the mean equals the stated efficiency

s.source: model/out/basin_index_check.json rowcrop_share_of_river_load (notes/fields_model.md: 1 - INRS point share x row-crop share of land load)

w.definition: share of the calendar year's measured (gap-filled) load passing Jan-Jul and Oct-Dec, i.e. the fall-to-July drainage window cover crops act on

path_b_learned.definition: relative change of the simulated median concentration when the causal bare share is cut by X (relative) on Oct 15-May 31, all cover features recomputed (model/river.py perturb_cover + predict)
path_b_learned.spread: bootstrap refits over training years (sensitivity.json, 5-95%, split-normal) + SD of the median/p10/p90 models' responses
path_b_learned.caveat: Historical bare-share variation is overwhelmingly seasonal (bare in winter/spring, green in summer) and its year-to-year differences are driven by weather (planting/green-up timing, harvest date), not by cover-crop adoption, which stayed at single-digit % of cropland. The model therefore never saw a watershed with much more winter living cover, so the learned sensitivity is weakly identified: the monotone constraint fixes its sign (less bare soil never raises nitrate), but its size is uncertain and a 50% cut takes winter bare share far outside the training range, where trees extrapolate flat (
path_b_learned.note: the bootstrap spread does not capture the identification problem (historic cover variation is seasonal), so inverse-variance weights favour this path; path-only results are reported for comparison

method_detail.blend: equal-weight mixture: 50% of Monte Carlo draws use the trial-prior path, 50% the learned-model path (so the range spans both lines of evidence); inverse-variance weights are reported only as a diagnostic because the learned path's bootstrap spread omits its identification problem

thresholds.plant_rule: plant runs when the 7-day mean of the average of the two rivers' measured nitrate exceeds 10.2 mg/L
thresholds.ban_rule: lawn-watering ban when, in the 06-08 (Jun-Aug) demand season, the plant proxy is on and the 7-day mean of BOTH rivers is above 10 mg/L
thresholds.cost_note: operating (O&M) cost only: 2025 O&M $1.6M / 112 days = low end; ~$16k/day at full capacity = high end. Capital ($0.6M in 2025; ~$40M expansion) is not avoided in the short run. Days avoided are shoulder-season days, when partial operation can cost less (facts: as low as ~$4k/day).
thresholds.source: Proxy operating rules fitted to 2025 CIWW plant/ban dates (KCCI, CIWW), tested on 2026; costs from CIWW 'What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?'

T_uncertainty.why: every threshold whose 2025 daily F1 is within 0.025 of the best fits 2025 about equally well, so the Monte Carlo draws T uniformly from them

plant.aug_nov_2026_note: No fall-2026 restart of the facility had been reported when facts were checked (facts.json plant_days_2026 notes), so these proxy days are probably false alarms; they are unverified either way.
plant.selection: aggregate and T chosen by daily F1 on 2025 only (ties: day count closest to 112, then lower T); 2026 never used for fitting

ban.rule: lawn-watering ban when, in the 06-08 (Jun-Aug) demand season, the plant proxy is on and the 7-day mean of BOTH rivers is above 10 mg/L
ban.T_source: not fitted: CIWW's 2025 lift rule says at least one source must read 10 mg/L or less (facts.json ban_lift_rule)

fitted_start_threshold_check.rule: Jun-Aug: the ban starts once the plant proxy is on and the lower river's 7-day mean exceeds T_start (fitted on 2025), and lasts while the plant proxy stays on
fitted_start_threshold_check.note: A start threshold fitted to 2025 matches 2025 almost exactly but finds no ban at all in 2026, when the ban came at lower nitrate (demand and capacity drove it). Over-fitted, so NOT used.

ban.caveat: A ban also depends on water demand (heat, lawn watering up to ~40% of summer demand), treatment capacity and the infiltration gallery, which this proxy cannot see. Ban counts use the all-customer Stage III window (2025: 56 days; homes 40). Treat ban-day changes as indicative.

caveats: Legacy nitrate: soils and groundwater hold years of nitrate, so a change on fields takes more than one season to show in the river; results describe the effect once it has developed, replayed on that year's weather.
Current adoption is already ~17% of Iowa corn+soy acres (statewide, secondary); X is ADDITIONAL acres.
Adopters are assumed to be typical fields; targeting leaky, tile-drained fields would do more, poor establishment less.
Trial efficiencies are mean drainage-concentration cuts with a large SD (28 +/- 26%); the learned river response is weakly identified (historic cover variation is mostly seasonal).
Plant and ban days come from proxy rules (the utility's rules are not public); 2026 test: see thresholds.calibration.
Cost avoided is operating cost only; capital is not avoided in the short run.
lb N kept = nitrate that would have reached the two gauges; on-farm retention is larger (in-stream removal not counted).
2026 is a partial year (data through 2026-11-13); 2026 nitrate data are partly provisional.
